recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not edit the historical release cache files for this R5-applied typo issue; they reflect older release history rather than current build-source guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-22140 is a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction for DocumentReference that asked to fix multiple typographical errors in the resource introduction/description text: "seralized" to "serialized", "patient centric" to "patient-centric", and "cliical" to "clinical", with the surrounding sentence changed from "so includes" to "it includes".
initial_application: The Jira comment records that the issue was already applied as GF#22140 in bc73aacdb442321d5100bbd6dc84e778bfe5bcad. That commit changed source/documentreference/documentreference-spreadsheet.xml from the misspelled wording to the corrected wording, alongside separate DocumentReference work for GF#17863. Later source refactoring in 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 moved the corrected text into source/documentreference/structuredefinition-DocumentReference.xml.
additional_context: DocumentReference is an active resource in source/fhir.ini, and the current active StructureDefinition source carries the corrected wording in both the resource description and the root element definition. A repository typo scan found the old wording only in tools/history/release4 and tools/history/release4b historical release caches, which preserve earlier published releases and are not current R6 source fixes. Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-22140 and DocumentReference typo terms found no discussion or minutes that change the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current build-scope DocumentReference source already contains the requested typo corrections.

related_jiras.note: The same historical implementation commit also mentioned GF#17863, but that appears to be separate DocumentReference work and was not needed to decide this typo-only seed.
